To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ADP and epinphrine cause a rapid increase in surface-bound calcium in human platelets.
ADP and epinphrine increase the amount of calcium bound to the platelets' surface membrane and that this bound calcium may play an important role in platelet activation.
ADP and epinine increase the amount of surface bound Ca2+, and that ADP and ephinephrine increase the rate of Ca exchange into the intracelluar pool.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of ADP on platelets.
elucidating the role of Ca2+ in the regulation of platelet function.
the role of calcium in blood platelet function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the platelets do not take up Ca2+ from the external medium, but rather, the Ca2+ that is present at the surface of the platelet is redistributed.
the Ca2+ binding to the surface of platelets may have a significant role in the platelet activation process.
ADP and epinphrine cause a rapid and transient increase in surface-bound Ca2+.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
platelets are not a simple system in which the Ca2+ influx is the sole mechanism of platelet activation.
platelet activation is not accompanied by an influx of Ca2+, but by a mobilization of Ca2+ from a surface-bound pool, which is then transferred to an intracellular pool.
the Ca2+ binding site is not only increased in the number of binding sites but also the number of binding site increases with the increase in the number binding sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca2+ binds to the platelet membrane and is not just passively bound.
the amount of Ca(2+) bound to the surface of the platelets increases with activation.
platelets are a rich source of calcium.
